concept: Dialog is a small appliance body that rises in front of the room to ask one question about a device, with plastic keys at the bottom and at most one orange key for the answer that acts.

default_to_avoid.pattern: centred white modal dialog with a 12px radius, an X in the corner and a dim black overlay (MUI Dialog, Radix Dialog)
default_to_avoid.why_not: The white card and soft shadow from above are the surface NEVER rule in FORM.md, and the corner X is a second way out that competes with Cancel.

default_to_avoid.pattern: modal dialog that scales and fades in with a staggered entry of its contents
default_to_avoid.why_not: P6 allows no entry choreography; only the change of state moves, so the sheet rises once and its contents arrive with it.

references.source: Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a lid that opens to show one panel of controls, then closes over them
Braun ET 66 calculator (Dietrich Lubs, 1987): body-coloured keys in a row with one coloured key for the main action
WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices, Dialog (Modal) pattern: focus moves in, Escape closes, focus returns to the opener

derivation.consequence: capped so large panels do not swell into pillows
derivation.form: The sheet's radius is corner.panel, the cap of the unit ratio, because every dialog is wider than the cap needs.

derivation.consequence: radius nests in the body (inner = outer − inset)
derivation.form: Anything nested in the sheet takes the radius corner.panel minus gap.inset, exposed to children as --dialog-inner.

derivation.consequence: orange appears once per unit, on the primary control's body only
derivation.form: The actions row holds plastic keys and at most one Button kind primary; the sheet itself never paints orange.

derivation.consequence: sits where the hand expects it (lower or right of the display)
derivation.form: Actions sit at the bottom of the sheet, aligned to the inline end, so the last key in reading order is the main one.

derivation.consequence: fast in, slow out, through the state motion tokens
derivation.form: The sheet and scrim arrive over motion.enter on the enter easing and leave over the longer motion.exit on the exit easing.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: Only opacity and a short rise of motion.rise move, all parts at once, and nothing moves under reduced motion.

options.name: floating unit, keys bottom-right, docks to the bottom edge on phones
display-led, question printed in an LCD window
docked bottom sheet on every screen, keys stacked

variants.reason: A keeps the sheet a unit of its own near the opener with the main key lower right (P1); B spends the display window on a question when P2 keeps the window for a device's state, and C glues a wide bar to the bottom of a laptop screen, so A takes C's docked shape only on phones.

root.why: The sheet is a body of matte plastic with the capped panel radius and one light from the top left.

inline.why: A non-modal sheet sits in the flow of the page at a fixed place and covers nothing.

title.why: The question is printed at the title size in medium weight, so it is the first thing read.

description.why: The note under the question uses the secondary ink, which holds 4.5:1 on the plastic body.

content.why: Fields and extra text sit on the same inset line as the question, never floating mid-surface.

actions.why: Keys sit together at the bottom and inline end of the sheet, where the hand expects the main key.

data-state=open.why: The open sheet and its scrim arrive quickly on the enter easing, all parts at the same moment.

@media pointer: coarse.why: On a phone held upright the sheet docks to the bottom edge and its keys span the width, where the thumb is.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduced motion the sheet appears and leaves at once, with no rise and no fade.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the sheet keeps a real border, so its edge survives without the cast shadow.

opacity.why: The sheet and scrim fade in fast and fade out slower, so leaving reads as the end of the question.

transform.why: A short rise of a few pixels is the only travel, with no scale, no bounce and no stagger.
